findings.problem: The scene that answers its own title question ('Do the work on write or on read?') rushes the answer. 16 s carries seven captions and about ten quantities (1 write, 3 lookups, 5 copies, 4,600, 300,000, 65, 75, 345,000, 30,000,000, 87 s, 5 s). The payoff is the last beat: caption 'A celebrity needs 87 seconds: go hybrid.' starts at 13.6 s, but the red bar gets its '87 s' label only at about 14.3 s, the 'hybrid' tag lands at about 14.7 s and the two-way card (most users / celebrities) at about 15.3 s, and the scene's 0.3 s fade-out starts at 15.7 s. So the hybrid answer is fully on screen for under half a second, in two small text lines, and a first-time learner cannot take in why hybrid. The caption is also about 0.7 s ahead of the number it quotes, and at 13.5 s the new phase prints 'celebrity: 30,000,000 copies...' on top of the fading 'posts per second' phase.
findings.fix: Rebalance the scene. Cut phase B to about 3 s (one bar pair and the '65 reads per post' tag, then straight to 4,600 x 75), start the celebrity caption when '87 s' lands (about 14.4 s) and hold the finished hybrid card for at least 2.5 s. If that is not enough, lengthen the scene to about 19 s (the video becomes about 126 s, still under 130). Make the hybrid card the biggest thing on the stage (two cards about 300 x 150 each, one per role) and end on it. Fade phase B fully out before phase C text appears.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s8@13.5 (old and new text overlap), s8@13.8 (caption on, bar half full, no number), s8@14.7 (hybrid tag only), s8@15.4 (card), s8@15.6; caps [13.6, 15.95]; V.FADE 0.3 in engine.js.

findings.problem: 'Fault' and 'failure', the two words in the headline and the whole point of the scene, are never defined on screen. 'fault' is a small tag that sits beside one dot for under 2 s (about 3.3 to 5 s) and 'failure' exists only as the counter 'failures: 7'. A first-time learner sees orange dots, then red dots, but nothing says fault = one part breaks, failure = users get no answer, so 'Faults are normal, failures are not' has no anchor. House rule: define jargon on screen before it is used.
findings.fix: Add two permanent legend tags under the headline from about 3.0 s: an orange dot 'fault: one part breaks' and a red dot 'failure: users get no answer' (28 px, in the free right column above the 'disk faults' stat or under the field), and drop the transient 'fault' tag. Keep the red/orange roles the legend states for the rest of the scene.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s5@1.2 (no definition), s5@3.3 (transient 'fault' tag), s5@5.2 and s5@6.8 ('failures: 7' with no definition), s5@11.3.

findings.problem: The maintenance beat does not show what its caption says. 'Even repairs take it offline.' (8.1 to 9.9 s) lands a grey wrench on a server that is already dead and red from the crash, so it reads as 'someone is fixing the crashed server', not 'a planned repair also needs downtime'. The grey wrench on pale red is also the weakest icon in the scene, and the third tag appears only at 8.3 s.
findings.fix: Revive the server to green with traffic flowing (about 7.9 s), then let the wrench arrive, the server go grey 'down' and the stream stop, and the 'maintenance: repairs need downtime' tag pop at the same moment (small tag 'planned' near the wrench). Colour the wrench orange or blue so it is visible on the pink card.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s2@7.8 (dead server, 'One crash...'), s2@8.6 and s2@9.5 (wrench on an already red, crossed server).

findings.problem: The two answer cards sit at the bottom left and right, directly under the London card, the 'buyer' icon and the New York card, so 'stay consistent: no answer' (orange card, bottom left) reads as London's or the buyer's reaction. The whole scene is about New York's choice. The 'refused' state is only an orange cross glyph floating above the customer's head (it looks like a stray mark), with no reply drawn back to the customer, whereas the available branch does send a '5' back (so the two branches are drawn differently). Both cards also arrive one after the other for the same customer, so they look like two events, not two alternative choices.
findings.fix: Frame the cards as New York's options: a small header tag 'New York must choose' above both, or place the two cards side by side under the New York card (x 486 to 906) with the customer between them. Draw the refusal as a reply bubble from New York back to the customer ('no answer', orange) mirroring the '5' reply of the other branch, and replace the floating cross by that bubble. Run the two choices as 'either ... or' (second card replaces the first at the same place) or show both with a small 'or' between them.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s3@7.2 (cross above customer, card under London), s3@8.5 (card under buyer), s3@9.5 and s3@10.5 (reply 5 for the other branch).

findings.problem: 'Consistent' and 'available' are in the headline and on both cards but are defined only by what New York does ('refuse to answer', 'answer, maybe stale'). A first-time learner does not learn that consistent = every copy shows the same value (never wrong) and available = always answers. The scene also opens with two copies and a link with no reason for them: nothing connects it to scene 2 (one crash stops everything), so why there are two copies is unexplained.
findings.fix: Under each card header add a short definition tag in the same colour: 'copies always agree' and 'always answers' (28 px). Rewrite caption 1 so it ties to scene 2, for example 'Fix a crash: keep a copy in each city.' (about 17 characters per second at 2.2 s), and keep 'link' on the wire.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s3@2.2 (two copies, no reason), s3@8.5 and s3@11.3 (cards without definitions); scene-02 end state s2@9.5.

findings.problem: Trade-off numbering and flow. Scene 3's kicker says 'TRADE-OFF 1' but there is never a 'trade-off 2' on screen: the second trade-off of the lecture (scale up or scale out, scene 9) is labelled 'SCALABILITY'. The learner is promised a series that does not arrive. Scene 8 is also introduced as 'CASE STUDY: TIMELINES' with no earlier mention of a case study, and 'TRADE-OFF 1' is followed straight by 'BUILDING BLOCKS' with no bridge.
findings.fix: Change the scene 9 kicker to 'TRADE-OFF 2' (the headline already poses the choice) and, if the kicker has to stay generic, rename scene 3's to 'TRADE-OFF'. Optionally add the bridge caption 'Next: the parts every data app needs.' as the first caption of scene 4 (it fits the 1.5 s before the first caption).
findings.evidence: scene-03 kicker (s3@2.2), scene-09 kicker (s9@4.0), scene-08 kicker (s8@3.4).

findings.problem: Too fast and too sparse. Four ideas in 13 s, about 2.5 to 3 s each. The cache gets 3.1 s for two requests (miss then hit) and the caption quoting '2 ms, not 100' starts at 4.4 s while the cache panel shows only the first request and the 'miss' tag (the '100 ms' tag lands at about 5.7 s and '2 ms' at about 6.7 s), so the caption is up to 2 s ahead of its picture. The database panel uses 2.6 s for the weakest picture (a packet goes in and a second packet comes out; the 'today' and 'tomorrow' tags are static labels in the top row, not tied to anything moving), and the figures are small (the database 110 px, the cache pieces 70 px) so each 450 x 290 panel is under half filled while the other three panels wait empty.
findings.fix: Cut the database panel to about 1.6 s and give the cache about 4.5 s: hold the first miss for at least 1 s, show the copy dropping into the cache, then the hit, and start caption 2 when '100 ms' has landed (about 5.7 s). Make the 'today'/'tomorrow' tags light up in turn on the way in and on the way out (packet goes in under 'today', comes out under 'tomorrow'). Enlarge the figures to fill their panels (database about 150 px, cache card about 150 x 100). Start caption 3 only after '20 checks' has finished counting (it reads '0 checks' at 7.9 s).
findings.evidence: ds-1 s4@2.8 (db panel), s4@4.6 and s4@5.8 (cache before '2 ms' exists), s4@6.8 (both labels), s4@7.9 (index bar reads '0 checks' while caption says '20 checks').

findings.problem: Stage balance. For the first 4.9 s the whole right column (x 524 to 988) is empty except the 'disk faults' stat, so the figure sits on the left half and the day counter runs on a lopsided stage. The 10,000 disks are 4 px dots, so the field reads as green texture and the learner cannot tell that each dot is a disk, only that a few orange ones appear; the day counter also steps every 0.42 s, so the 'about one a day' rhythm is hard to feel.
findings.fix: Show the two row cards in outline from the start (fade them in grey at 1.3 s, fill them at 4.9 s) or move the stat under the field, and slow the day steps to about 0.55 s (the total week 3.9 s). Optionally zoom a tiny corner of the field (6 x 6 disks) in a small inset so a dot is visibly a disk.

findings.problem: The core of the scene, the overload cascade, goes by too fast to follow. After the second death at 4.6 s the survivors' numbers 105, 140, 210 and 420 change at deaths at 6.8, 7.65, 8.3 and 9.0 s, so 140, 210 and 420 are each visible for about 0.4 to 0.5 s, together with the '+35', '+70' and '+210' chips that fly across and the stat 'alive' counting down. A first-time learner can see servers falling but cannot read why (each death hands its load to fewer servers).
findings.fix: Spend about 1 s per death for the first two overloaded servers (105 to 140 to 210) and let the last two run quicker, or stretch the scene by 2 s (video about 125 s). Hold each new per-server number at least 0.8 s, and keep the '+N' chip on screen until the number it adds to has finished changing.

findings.problem: Two unclear pieces of the figure. (1) 'each takes 100' is the capacity, but it is a small grey tag in the top-right corner far from the servers and the wording is ambiguous ('takes' could mean it currently carries 100); the idea 'over 100 = overloaded' therefore depends on the caption. (2) The bug beat is abrupt: at 9.5 s all six servers revive to 70, a bug icon arrives and they all die, but nothing says why this differs from the hardware deaths just seen (the same software runs on every server). The '+N' chips and 'alive' counter are unexplained decoration.
findings.fix: Reword the capacity tag 'can handle 100' and place it as a dashed limit line across the server meters (or a '100' mark on each meter), turning orange when exceeded. For the bug beat add a tag under the row, 'same software on all six', before the bug lands, and keep the final 'all fail together' tag as is. Label the first '+N' chip once, for example 'shares its load'.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s6@1.0 (tag at far right), s6@5.4 (tag turns orange), s6@9.6 (revival), s6@10.2 (bug), s6@11.5.

findings.problem: Colour role for a dead part is inconsistent. A dead disk (a fault) is orange in scene 5, and red is kept for 'failures: 7'. But a single dead server is red with a red cross in scenes 2, 6 and 9 (D1.server 'down'), even where the point is that the fault is tolerated ('fault tolerated' green tag in scene 6, '88% left' in scene 9). The learner learns in scene 5 that orange = fault and red = failure, then sees a tolerated fault drawn in the failure colour.
findings.fix: Pick one convention and apply it everywhere: a dead component = orange (fault), with red reserved for service-level failure ('dropped', 'all down', 'no answer'); or keep red for dead things and make the scene 5 disks red and the failure marks a darker 'service down' treatment. The first option needs only a 'fault' state in D1.server (orange tint, orange cross) used when the survivors are still serving.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s5@7.8 (orange dead disk), s6@3.6 (red dead server, green 'fault tolerated'), s9@7.4 (red dead server beside '88% left').

findings.problem: Two undefined terms and a missing frame for the SCALABILITY scenes. 'ms' (milliseconds) appears in scene 4 ('2 ms, not 100', '100 ms') and scene 7 ('response time, ms', 'average 250') without ever being spelled out, and 'response time' itself is only an axis label. Scenes 7, 9 carry the kicker SCALABILITY but scalability is only ever defined in scene 2 as 'only so big', so scene 7 (spread of response times) does not obviously connect to scalability (more load, slower and more varied answers) or to scene 9 (add machines).
findings.fix: Spell it once: 'ms = thousandths of a second' as a small grey tag in scene 4's cache panel and use 'response time (ms)' in scene 7. In scene 7 add a 28 px tag over the plot 'more load: slower answers' or open with 'scalable = still fast as load grows' for the first caption; in scene 9 reuse the same words.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s4@7.2 ('2 ms', '100 ms'), s7@2.5 (axis 'response time, ms'), s7@9.8; kickers on scenes 7 and 9.

findings.problem: Vocabulary the learner has not been given. 'Timeline' (the headline's case study and 'Ana's timeline') is never defined as 'the posts of the people you follow'; the same thing is called 'tweets' ('all tweets'), 'posts' (caption, 'posts per second') and 'timeline reads'; and in approach 2 Ana appears twice, as a mailbox in the column and as 'Ana's timeline' on the right, with no statement that the mailbox is her timeline. 'Mailbox', 'merge on read' and 'copy on write' are bare tags. Also 'reads' counts lookups in phase A (3) and timeline views in phase B (300,000), which the facts review flagged.
findings.fix: Use one word ('post') everywhere, retitle the store card 'all posts', add a one-time tag 'timeline = posts from people you follow' under Ana's timeline at 2.6 s, and merge the two Ana elements in approach 2 (fly the copy into Ana's timeline card directly, or label the mailbox column 'timelines (one each)'). Rename the approach tags to the lesson's terms ('merge on read', 'fan-out on write'; see the facts review).
findings.evidence: ds-1 s8@3.4 (all tweets, Ana's timeline), s8@6.4 (mailbox Ana plus Ana's timeline), s8@8.8, s8@12.6 ('posts / s').

findings.problem: The scene states, but never shows, why scale up costs more. The 8x machine is only about 1.6 times as wide as one 1x machine (so 'one bigger machine' does not look 8 times bigger or visibly packed with power), the cost bars have no scale or zero mark, and the learner is handed 4-digit pound figures to the pound (£34,297, £8,800) with no reason (the facts review notes these come from a cost model). 'Power' in 'need 8x the power' is never defined. After the failure beat ('capacity left 0% / 88%') nothing says why 88 (7 of 8 machines left).
findings.fix: Draw the big machine as an obvious block of eight (a 2 x 4 grid of 1x tiles fused into one body, double the card size) and add one tag 'bigger costs more per unit' over the scale-up cost. Show costs as '4x' / '1x' next to the pound figures or round them in the caption ('about four times'), and write '7 of 8 left' under '88%'. Add the word 'capacity' once ('need 8x the capacity').
findings.evidence: ds-1 s9@4.0 (cards and costs), s9@7.4 (capacity left 0% / 88%), s9@10.8.

findings.problem: The scene opens (0.3 to 3.2 s) with three text-and-icon cards, 'easy to run', 'easy to understand', 'easy to change' plus operability, simplicity, evolvability, which is exactly a bullet list: nothing moves, and the three jargon words are never used again. The rest of the scene demonstrates only the third kind (swap one database), yet the headline 'Maintainable systems are easy to change' narrows the three kinds to one, so 'easy to run' and 'easy to understand' are named but never shown.
findings.fix: Make the intro a picture: three tiny scenes (a server with a green on/off switch for run, a tangled 20-line mesh being straightened for understand, a wrench changing one box for change) or cut the three cards to 1.5 s as a legend row that stays small above the diagram with the active one lit while it is shown (mesh = understand, 'replace it' = change). Retitle to 'Maintainable: easy to run, understand and change', or keep the headline and say in the first caption that this scene shows the third.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s10@1.2 and s10@2.4 (text cards), s10@3.4 (cards fading), s10@5.0, s10@7.6.

findings.problem: The finished comparison disappears at the end. The last frame shows 'connections 9' and 'to edit 1' alone; the earlier 20 and 5 are gone, so the improvement (20 to 9, 5 to 1) has to be remembered. The wrench badges on the five services are about 30 px circles and read as keys at this size.
findings.fix: Keep a struck-through grey 20 and 5 next to the final 9 and 1 (or show '20 -> 9' and '5 -> 1'), and enlarge the wrench badges to about 44 px.
findings.evidence: ds-1 s10@7.6 (20 and 5), s10@11.2 (final frame), s10@7.6 (badges).

findings.problem: Caption density. Nominal speeds are 15 to 18 characters per second, but each caption fades in and out for 0.25 s, so the effective reading time is 18 to 22 characters per second for about a third of the captions (scene 10 all five, scene 8 captions 3, 5 and 6, scene 6 caption 2, scene 3 captions 4 and 5, scene 5 captions 4 and 5, scene 2 caption 3).
findings.fix: Lengthen the windows of the fastest ones by 0.3 to 0.5 s where the picture allows (scene 10 has 0.4 s of slack before the first caption, scene 8 can borrow from phase B), or shorten the text: 'Now only the layer changes.' to 'Only the layer changes.', 'Every service talks to every database.' to 'Every service uses every database.', 'Copy on write: 345,000 a second.' to '345,000 writes a second.'.
findings.evidence: Computed from caps arrays in scene-*.js and the 0.25 s ramp in engine.js line 167.

findings.problem: Empty or lopsided stage areas. Scene 2: the lower-left (x 70 to 600, y 560 to 860) is blank until the tags pop at 4.6, 6.4 and 8.3 s. Scene 3: the lower third (y 700 to 940) is blank until the first answer card at 7.4 s. Scene 7: the finished plot uses only the top half of the stage (dots about 170 px tall) with a blank band beneath the 'quick' and 'slow' tags. Scene 8 phase C: bars and card take the top 60 per cent and the bottom is empty.
findings.fix: Where the layout allows, lift the final cards and tags higher or enlarge the figure (scene 7 histogram height 300 to 380 px; scene 3 move the answer cards up to y 380 and make them 190 px tall; scene 8 phase C bars 80 px high).

findings.problem: The recap holds three points (faults, add machines, easy to run/understand/change) but leaves out the two things the video spent most time on: the consistency-versus-availability trade-off (11.5 s) and the building blocks / response-time spread, so the last frame does not mirror the lecture's second half; scene 11 also has no on-screen caption, so the order of the three rows is the only cue.
findings.fix: Optional: keep three rows but change the first to 'Plan for faults, keep copies' with the existing pictogram and add 'consistent or available' as a one-line sub-label under row 1, or leave as is and accept the short recap.
